paragraphs.source_en: Of late, I have taken up exercise. Some ignorant fellows may abuse me roundly, saying that I am only a cat and yet have the presumption to go in for exercise; here I must state my view. Take those who scold me, for example: until quite recently they did not even understand what exercise meant, and supposed eating and sleeping to be their sole heavenly calling. Those fortunate enough to be called persons of rank would sit with hands tucked in their sleeves, never lifting their half-rotten backsides from the cushion, and regard this as the dignity of a gentleman. They lived in smug self-satisfaction. All the later nonsense that came one after another, saying one should exercise, drink milk, take cold baths, jump into the sea, or in summer go into the mountains and live for a while on mist and clouds, is a recent fever transmitted from the West to sacred Japan, a disease fit to be classed with plague, consumption, and nervous prostration. I was born only last year and am just one year old this year, so of course I cannot remember what things were like when human beings first began to suffer from this malady. Not only that, at the time I was certainly not yet caught up in this frivolous current of the world. Still, one year for a cat may fairly be said to equal ten years for a human being. Although we cats live only one-half or one-third as long as people, judging from the full development of a cat's mind in so short a time, it is a grave mistake to reckon human years and feline years as equivalent. In my own case, the fact that I possess such lofty opinions before even reaching one year and a few months is proof enough. The master's third daughter is said to be three by the old count, but as for the development of her intellect, why, she is astonishingly dull. She knows nothing except crying, wetting the bed, and drinking milk. Compared with me, who grieves for the world and rails at the times, she is innocence itself. Since I am that sort of cat, there is nothing in the least strange about my pondering exercise, sea bathing, and change-of-air cures within my breast. If anyone finds even these matters surprising, it must be because human beings have two fewer legs than cats. Humans have been fools from long ago; that is why only recently have they begun to proclaim the meaning of exercise and chatter on about the benefits of sea bathing as if they had made a great discovery. As for me, I understood such things from birth. First, as to why seawater is good for the body, one need only go to the shore and it becomes clear at once. One cannot know how many fish there are in that vast sea, but not a single one has ever fallen ill and gone to a doctor; they all swim about in lively health. If it were ill, could it still swim? If it died, it would certainly float up. Thus a fish's passing is called “floating up,” a bird's demise is called “falling down,” and a human being's extinction is styled “lying stiff.” Ask anyone who has been abroad whether, when crossing the Indian Ocean, he ever saw a dead fish, and surely everyone will answer no. Naturally they must answer so.

paragraphs.source_zh: 在下近来开始运动了。也许有些无知之徒会把我臭骂一通，说我大不了是只猫儿，竟然也搞起什么运动，这里我得表示我的意见。就拿骂我的人来说吧，他们直到最近还不理解运动为何意，只知道吃和睡是唯一的天职。那些有幸被称为贵人的，总是袖着两只手，让那快要糜烂的屁股永远不离开坐垫，认为这就是做老爷们的尊荣。他们过着自我得意的生活。以后接二连三出现的应该运动呀、提倡喝牛奶呀、进行冷水浴呀、应该跳进海去、夏季应该去山里同烟霞为伴等等，所有这些无聊的提法，都是从西方传到神国日本来的，是近期才发生的一种热，甚至被认为是和鼠疫、肺结核、神经衰弱不相上下的热病。我是去年生的，今年才一岁，当然不可能记住人开始患此病症时的情景。不仅如此，那时，我肯定还没有卷入这种浮薄的世风中。不过猫儿一岁，可以说顶得上人的十岁。甭看我们猫儿的寿命比人要短两三倍，但从一只猫儿在短期内头脑的充分发达情况来看，把人的岁数和猫儿的岁数同等来看是极端错误的。就以我来说，现在还不到一岁零几个月，就有如此的高见，这就足以说明问题了。主人的第三个女儿，据说虚岁已经三岁，但从智力的发达来讲，啊呀，那简直是迟钝极啦。除了哭、尿床和吃奶以外，什么也不懂。将她和愤世嫉俗的我来比较，她简直是幼稚到极点啦。正因为我是这样的一只猫儿，所以我把运动、海水浴、转地疗养的兴趣都放在心上考虑，这是丝毫不足为怪的。如果对这些事儿也感到奇怪，那肯定是因为人比猫儿少两条腿的缘故。人很早就是二百五，所以直到最近才开始鼓吹运动的意义，喋喋不休地讲海水浴的益处，好像这是一项伟大的发明。其实这类事儿，我生来就懂得。先说海水为什么会对身体有好处吧，只要你去一趟海滨就立刻会明白。在那辽阔的大海里究竟有多少鱼固然无法知道，不过，从来没有一条鱼生病去找医生的，都是活蹦乱跳地游来游去。如果有病，它还能游吗？如果死了那肯定要漂起来。所以鱼逝世，称作“漂上来”，鸟的薨去，呼做“掉下来”，人的寂灭号称“挺尸”。你可以去问问出过洋的人，当他们横渡印度洋时有没有看见过死鱼，肯定任何人都会回答说没有。他们当然要这样回答。

paragraphs.source_en: No matter how many times one goes back and forth across the sea, no one has ever seen a fish that had stopped breathing, or rather, since it is a fish, not “stopped breathing” but “breathed its last in the tide,” floating up. In that surging, boundless ocean, even if one rode a steamship and searched day and night, one would not find a single fish floating up. From this inference one may immediately pronounce that fish are remarkably robust. Then, if one asks why fish are so robust? This too is something humans do not understand, though the reason is simple and can be grasped at once. It is because fish are always drinking seawater and taking sea baths. The efficacy of sea bathing is thus so plainly evident in fish. Since it is beneficial to fish, it naturally ought to be beneficial to humans as well. When, in 1750, Dr. Richard Russell issued his extravagant advertisement saying that if one jumped into the sea at Brighton all diseases would be instantly cured, one may certainly laugh at him for advertising it far too late. Though we are cats, once the proper time arrives, we too may go to the shore at Kamakura. For the present, however, it will not do; in all things there is a matter of timing. Just as the Japanese before the Meiji Restoration died without experiencing the efficacy of seawater, cats today have not yet reached the time when they may plunge naked into the sea. Haste is sure to make a botch of things. For example, so long as a cat abandoned on the Tsukiji shore has not yet safely returned home, I shall not recklessly go and leap into the sea. Until the law of evolution has given us cats adequate resistance to raging waves and stormy billows, in other words, until common speech says not “the cat has died” but “the cat has floated up,” sea bathing will be difficult to practice.

units.source_en: No matter how many times one goes back and forth across the sea, no one has ever seen a fish that had stopped breathing, or rather, since it is a fish, not “stopped breathing” but “breathed its last in the tide,” floating up.
units.source_zh: 不管你在海上经过多少个来回，也不会有人看见过一条鱼会是停止呼吸——不，说“停止呼吸”不妥当，因为是鱼嘛，应该说是在潮水中咽气——漂上来的。

units.source_en: In that surging, boundless ocean, even if one rode a steamship and searched day and night, one would not find a single fish floating up.
units.source_zh: 在那波涛汹涌、漫无际涯的大海中，就是坐上蒸汽船不分昼夜地去寻找，也不会发现一条鱼会漂上来。

units.source_en: From this inference one may immediately pronounce that fish are remarkably robust.
units.source_zh: 由此推论下去，可以立即下断语说鱼是极其壮实的。

units.source_en: Then, if one asks why fish are so robust?
units.source_zh: 那么要问鱼为什么那样壮实？

units.source_en: This too is something humans do not understand, though the reason is simple and can be grasped at once.
units.source_zh: 这也是人所不了解的，其实道理很简单，立刻能弄明白的。

units.source_en: It is because fish are always drinking seawater and taking sea baths.
units.source_zh: 那就是因为鱼始终饮用海水，进行海水浴的缘故。

units.source_en: The efficacy of sea bathing is thus so plainly evident in fish.
units.source_zh: 海水浴对鱼的功效是如此的显著。

units.source_en: Since it is beneficial to fish, it naturally ought to be beneficial to humans as well.
units.source_zh: 既然对鱼儿有益处，那么对人也自然应该是有益处。

units.source_zh: 一七五〇年里查德·拉塞尔博士刊登了一则夸大的广告，谈只要跳进布赖顿海水浴场，百病可以马上全部治愈，你当然可以嘲笑他的广告刊登得太晚。

units.source_en: Though we are cats, once the proper time arrives, we too may go to the shore at Kamakura.
units.source_zh: 我们虽然是些猫儿，但只要时机成熟，我们也可以去镰仓海滨。

units.source_en: For the present, however, it will not do; in all things there is a matter of timing.
units.source_zh: 现在还不行，万事都有个时机问题。

units.source_en: Just as the Japanese before the Meiji Restoration died without experiencing the efficacy of seawater, cats today have not yet reached the time when they may plunge naked into the sea.
units.source_zh: 正如明治维新前的日本人未能体验到海水的功效就死掉一样，今天的猫儿还未到可以裸体跳进海水的时机。

units.source_en: Haste is sure to make a botch of things.
units.source_zh: 急于干就必然出现差错。

units.source_en: For example, so long as a cat abandoned on the Tsukiji shore has not yet safely returned home, I shall not recklessly go and leap into the sea.
units.source_zh: 譬如今天，在被抛弃到筑地海岸的猫儿还未能平安回到家之前，我可不会不顾一切地去跳海。

units.source_en: Until the law of evolution has given us cats adequate resistance to raging waves and stormy billows, in other words, until common speech says not “the cat has died” but “the cat has floated up,” sea bathing will be difficult to practice.
units.source_zh: 在进化法则还未能使我们这些猫儿对狂澜怒涛产生适当的抵抗力之前——换言之，在一般用语中还未把“猫死了”说成是“猫漂上来了”之前——海水浴是很难进行的。

paragraphs.source_zh: 不管你在海上经过多少个来回，也不会有人看见过一条鱼会是停止呼吸——不，说“停止呼吸”不妥当，因为是鱼嘛，应该说是在潮水中咽气——漂上来的。在那波涛汹涌、漫无际涯的大海中，就是坐上蒸汽船不分昼夜地去寻找，也不会发现一条鱼会漂上来。由此推论下去，可以立即下断语说鱼是极其壮实的。那么要问鱼为什么那样壮实？这也是人所不了解的，其实道理很简单，立刻能弄明白的。那就是因为鱼始终饮用海水，进行海水浴的缘故。海水浴对鱼的功效是如此的显著。既然对鱼儿有益处，那么对人也自然应该是有益处。一七五〇年里查德·拉塞尔博士刊登了一则夸大的广告，谈只要跳进布赖顿海水浴场，百病可以马上全部治愈，你当然可以嘲笑他的广告刊登得太晚。我们虽然是些猫儿，但只要时机成熟，我们也可以去镰仓海滨。现在还不行，万事都有个时机问题。正如明治维新前的日本人未能体验到海水的功效就死掉一样，今天的猫儿还未到可以裸体跳进海水的时机。急于干就必然出现差错。譬如今天，在被抛弃到筑地海岸的猫儿还未能平安回到家之前，我可不会不顾一切地去跳海。在进化法则还未能使我们这些猫儿对狂澜怒涛产生适当的抵抗力之前——换言之，在一般用语中还未把“猫死了”说成是“猫漂上来了”之前——海水浴是很难进行的。
